# Baghdad 830 – Agriculture & food

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Three-field rotation** [`three_field_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/three_field_system.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The Sawad grows winter wheat and barley and, where water lasts, summer rice, millet, sesame and cotton. Much land lies fallow every other year to rest and to let the salt wash out. Water, not rotation, sets the rhythm. Local: estates and tax lands of the Sawad (central and southern Iraq).
- **Legumes and green manure** [`legumes_green_manure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/legumes_green_manure.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Lentils, chickpeas and broad beans are field crops, and fodder crops are grown for the horses of the army and the court. That a bean crop feeds the next grain crop is farmer's lore at best, with no explanation.
- **Four-course rotation with clover and turnips** [`crop_rotation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crop_rotation.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. Clover and turnips mean nothing here. Farmers alternate winter and summer crops on irrigated plots; a fixed fodder course that ends fallow would need more water than the canals give.
- **Manure, compost and night soil** [`manure_compost_night_soil`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/manure_compost_night_soil.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Dung, ashes and town refuse go to the market gardens and orchards around Baghdad; pigeon droppings are prized for melons. Nobody links night soil in gardens to the city's fevers and fluxes. Local: market gardens and palm groves along the Tigris and the Sarat and Isa canals.
- **Liming and marling of sour soils** [`liming_marling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/liming_marling.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Iraqi alluvium is alkaline and salty, not sour; lime would do harm. The real enemy is salt brought up by irrigation without drainage, which is slowly ruining the south.
- **Mineral fertiliser (guano, phosphate, potash, nitrate)** [`mineral_fertiliser`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mineral_fertiliser.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. No idea of plant nutrients. Nitre and potash are known as substances, not as food for plants.
- **Terracing and soil conservation** [`terracing_soil_conservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/terracing_soil_conservation.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Terraces are old in Yemen and the Iranian mountains. Iraq is flat; its problems are silting canals and salinisation, met by dredging and abandoning spent land rather than by drainage. Elsewhere: Yemen, ancient terraced highlands.
- **Heavy mouldboard plough** [`heavy_plough`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heavy_plough.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. The ox-drawn ard with an iron share suits light, stoneless alluvium and is the right tool here. A heavy mouldboard plough would bring salt up and bog down in irrigated fields.
- **Horse collar and breast-strap harness** [`horse_collar_harness`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/horse_collar_harness.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Oxen pull under a yoke; goods move on camels, mules and donkeys, and wheeled carts are rare in the Middle East since the camel replaced them in late antiquity. A collar has few customers. Elsewhere: Tang China, breast-strap and collar harness.
- **Seed drill** [`seed_drill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/seed_drill.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Grain is broadcast by hand and ploughed in. Seed tubes on the plough are old in India and were used in ancient Mesopotamia, but nobody here uses them now. Elsewhere: India, seed-tube ploughs.
- **Scythe and grain cradle** [`scythe_cradle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scythe_cradle.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Grain is cut with the sickle by gangs of labourers; long blades for fodder are known. Labour is cheap, so a faster blade is a modest gain.
- **Mechanical reaper and threshing machine** [`reaper_thresher`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reaper_thresher.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Oxen and donkeys tread the sheaves or drag a threshing sledge studded with flints; winnowing is by hand against the wind. No machine.
- **Selective breeding of plants and animals** [`selective_breeding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selective_breeding.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Arab horse lines are recorded by descent and prized; camels are bred for riding or load. Date palms are propagated from offshoots of good females and pollinated by hand, so growers already select deliberately. Local: date growers of Basra and the Sawad; horse dealers and the caliph's stables.
- **Grafting of fruit trees and vines** [`grafting_fruit_trees`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grafting_fruit_trees.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Gardeners graft citrus, apricots, pears and vines routinely, following Persian practice and Greek farming books known through Syriac. Local: palace gardens on the east bank (Shammasiyya, Rusafa).
- **Irrigation and water lifting (canal, qanat, shaduf, noria)** [`irrigation_water_lifting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/irrigation_water_lifting.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The Sawad lives on a Sasanian canal grid (Nahrawan, Nahr Isa, Sarat), with sluices, shadufs, animal-driven saqiyas and river-driven norias. Iran waters its towns by qanats. Upkeep is a state task; neglect and salt are the threats. Local: Nahr Isa and Sarat canals, Baghdad; Nahrawan canal east of the Tigris; officials who assess and repair the canals. Elsewhere: Khurasan and Fars, qanats.
- **Wet rice (paddy) cultivation** [`wet_rice_cultivation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wet_rice_cultivation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Rice is a staple around Wasit, in the southern marshes (the Batiha) and in Khuzistan; the poor of Basra eat rice bread. It is spreading west to Egypt and beyond. Local: Wasit and the Batiha marshes; Khuzistan.
- **Polders – land reclamation with dikes and wind pumps** [`windmill_drainage_land_reclamation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill_drainage_land_reclamation.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. The great marshes south of Wasit (the Batiha) grew, by the Arab geographers' account, when the Tigris broke its dikes in late Sasanian times; Umayyad governors reclaimed some land. Water is lifted by animals. Windmills are a rumour from Sistan. Local: the Batiha marshes (Zutt rebels hold parts until 834/835). Elsewhere: Sistan, windmills (reliably reported only from the 10th c.).
- **Fish ponds and carp polyculture** [`aquaculture_fish_ponds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aquaculture_fish_ponds.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Fish come from the Tigris, the canals and the marshes. Palaces keep ornamental pools with fish; deliberate fish farming for food is not practised. Elsewhere: Tang China, carp ponds.
- **Crops of the Americas (potato, maize and others)** [`new_world_crops`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/new_world_crops.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. Nobody in the Old World knows of these plants. Elsewhere: the Americas.
- **Growing and storing potatoes** [`potato_cultivation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/potato_cultivation.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. No potatoes exist outside the Andes.

The principle applies to the date palm and to wheat; a single blight or locust year shows it.
- **The Columbian exchange (plants, animals and diseases across the Atlantic)** [`columbian_exchange`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/columbian_exchange.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low. The Old World exchange is the one under way here. Rice, sugar, cotton and citrus are moving west through the caliphate (how fast and how far is debated).
- **Food preservation (salting, drying, smoking, pickling)** [`food_preservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/food_preservation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Dates are dried and pressed into blocks or boiled to syrup (dibs); fish is salted and sun-dried; vegetables are pickled in vinegar; murri, a fermented barley sauce, is a staple of cookery; sugar and honey preserve fruit. Local: Basra date packers; cooks and confectioners of the court.
- **Canning (heat-preserving in sealed containers)** [`canning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/canning.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Glazed jars sealed with pitch or fat are used for oil and syrups. Heating a sealed jar to keep its contents is unknown.
- **Pasteurisation** [`pasteurisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pasteurisation.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Milk is soured or made into cheese; date wine and nabidh go off quickly in the heat, which matters to jurists who forbid them once fermented.
- **Grain storage and protection from pests and ergot** [`grain_storage_pest_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grain_storage_pest_control.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Grain is kept in pits, jars and state granaries; tax grain feeds the army and the capital. Weevils and rats are accepted losses. Ergot is no issue; rye is not grown.
- **Sea fisheries – stockfish, salt cod and cured herring** [`sea_fisheries_salt_cod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sea_fisheries_salt_cod.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Gulf fishermen salt and dry fish and small fry for the inland market. Cod and herring belong to seas nobody here has sailed. Elsewhere: the Gulf coast (Basra, Ubulla, Siraf).
- **Sugar from cane and from beet** [`sugar_cane_beet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sugar_cane_beet.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Cane is grown and boiled in Khuzistan, a crop since Sasanian times, and refined into loaves and rock candy (qand). Sugar is a luxury, a medicine and the base of court confectionery. Beet sugar is unknown. Local: Khuzistan cane fields (Ahvaz, Gondeshapur); sugar-sellers in the Baghdad markets.
- **Sericulture (silk raising)** [`sericulture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sericulture.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Silkworms are raised in Khurasan, Gurgan and Syria. Baghdad weaves silk, and state tiraz workshops embroider robes with the caliph's name. Local: tiraz workshops. Elsewhere: Merv and Gurgan, silk raising.
- **Movable-frame beehive** [`beekeeping_movable_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/beekeeping_movable_frame.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Bees are kept in clay-pipe and basket hives; honey is cut out by destroying the comb. Sugar competes with honey at the rich table.
- **Coffee, tea and cacao** [`coffee_tea_cacao`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coffee_tea_cacao.md) — K1, use none, make impossible, accept medium. Coffee grows wild in Ethiopia, unknown here. China merchants may mention that people there drink an infused herb taxed by the emperor; the first Arabic record of it is from c. 851.
